title: Elitewheels DRIVE II Review: Are They Overhyped?

takeaways.text: Wheels supplied by Elitewheels. The 50 mm pair weighed 1,322 g with tape (1,300 g claimed without); internal width 23.2 mm, external about 30.7 mm; 28 mm tires measured just over 30 mm.
Price rose from US$1,199 to US$1,299 for the second generation (September 2025), before the reviewer's discount code.
Bench checks: lateral true within 0.3 mm, near-perfect radial true, every spoke within 5% of average tension, centred hubs and clean rim interiors.
28 mm tires were the hardest he had ever fitted, needing levers, but seated with a floor pump without sealant; rims are a 'reduced hook' profile between hooked and hookless.
Very responsive and quick to accelerate, a little harsh on rough roads, and rock-solid above 70 km/h and in crosswinds; the conical-ratchet hub had no issues after about 800 km.

disclosure: The linked written review states that the manufacturer supplied the wheels. The description carries a 15% discount code and an affiliate disclosure.
summary: Indoor and mountain riding test of the Drive II 50D with a comparison to the first generation, plus checks of trueness, spoke tension and the rim interior. The linked written review identifies the 50 mm depth.
